Manager, Product Manager, Audit Insights & Innovation, AI and Data Engineering

Product Management at Capital One is a booming, vibrant craft that requires reimagining the status quo, finding value creation opportunities, and driving innovative and sustainable customer experiences through technology.

We believe our portfolio of businesses and investments in growth and transformation will result in a company with the scale, brand, capabilities, talent, and values to succeed as the digital revolution transforms our society and our industry.

Do you dream of well-designed and intuitive products and customer experiences? Do you want to be the one who introduces change to help tens of millions of customers make smarter financial choices? Do you want to change the way people manage their money? If you answered yes to all of these questions, then product management at Capital One may be a fit for you

About the Role and Team

The Audit Insights and Innovation (I&I) team at Capital One is at the cutting edge of AI, data management, and machine learning, to deliver key risk insights for internal auditors shaping the risk management landscape. You will join a cross-functional team dedicated to modernizing internal audit workflows, by working with full-stack engineering teams and dedicated UI/UX designers. Our team is building products that focus on surfacing critical, real-time insights for auditors throughout the audit lifecycle. As a Product Manager, you will bridge the gap between generative AI capabilities, enterprise-scale design, and specialized domain expertise, navigating a complex regulated landscape to deliver high-impact solutions. This high-visibility role offers the chance to build foundational AI-assisted auditing experiences at one of the nation's leading digital banks. You will own the vision and roadmap of your experience within the Audit Compass application, driving immediate value to auditors. To be successful in this role, you will have experience with understanding and building complex data pipelines and build foundational AI capabilities for all of audit engineering.

In this role, you’ll learn the essentials of being a product manager, and we’ll invest in you to grow in four key areas:

Human Centered
• You’ll collaborate with tech teams to build comprehensive acceptance criteria, identifying and elevating any need for additional research to define future feature design

• You'll breakdown business epics into features and further into user stories, driving your team towards lowest effort or Minimal Viable Product (MVP) for a valid feature test

Business Focused
• Demonstrating a growth mindset, you’ll effectively use hypothesis-driven assessment of data to ensure your product or feature delivers on real business needs

• You’ll own and prioritize feature development roadmaps, ensuring all necessary processes and procedures are followed to manage risk

Technology Driven
• You’ll work autonomously in an agile environment, to conduct research and develop features that utilize new and evolving technology

• You’ll collaborate with designers, technologists, data scientists and subject-matter experts to build cutting edge solutions to help customers

• You’ll deliver well-managed product platforms for customers by seeking to understand technology trends and architecture strategy

Transformational Leadership
• By actively participating in horizontal forums, you’ll harness a network of trusted relationships among tech teams, designers, key internal stakeholders and partner teams

• You’ll articulate a succinct product roadmap to deliver business value and share with w

• Intellectually Curious. You ask why, you explore, you're not afraid to blurt out your crazy idea or follow an email chain for weeks to find someone with an answer. Comfortable with ambiguity, a hunger to learn and a seeker of new challenges

• Communicator & Influencer. You can communicate complex ideas clearly regardless of your audience. Our team knows their priorities and why they’re doing what they’re doing. You always can rally associates to work with you

• Do-er. You’re biased toward action, you try things and sometimes you fail. You can get around roadblocks and stay focused on your goals. You’re well organized, able to multitask and able to prioritize your work

• Passionate & Customer Focus. You care about growing others and bringing them together around what’s possible. You get a thrill from the journey of building and shipping products, and you have a desire and ability to connect with our external or internal customers to fully understand their needs

• Learner. You have an appetite to learn new things or new technologies all while exhibiting humbleness when the time comes to ask for help

• Team Player. You enjoy working with diverse people and driving the team toward a common goal. You have the ability to put the team before yourself and establish long-lasting relationships

• A Bachelor's or Master’s Degree in a quantitative field (Statistics, Economics, Operations Research, Analytics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Information Systems or a related quantitative field), Business or Marketing

Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients

At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do.

Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. With our focus on four therapeutic areas –Oncology, Inflammation, General Medicine, and Rare Disease– we reach millions of patients each year. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline of medicines to treat cancer, heart disease, inflammatory conditions, rare diseases, and obesity and obesity-related conditions. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives.

Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career.

What are Trust Fund Positions?

Trust Fund positions are unique to the Smithsonian. They are paid for from a variety of sources, including the Smithsonian endowment, revenue from our business activities, donations, grants and contracts. Trust employees are not part of the civil service, nor does trust fund employment lead to Federal status. The salary ranges for trust positions are generally the same as for federal positions and in many cases trust and federal employees work side by side. Trust employees have their own benefit program, which may include Health, Dental & Vision Insurance, Life Insurance, Transit/Commuter Benefits, Accidental Death and Dismemberment Insurance, Annual and Sick Leave, Family Friendly Leave, 403b Retirement Plan, Discounts for Smithsonian Memberships, Museum Stores and Restaurants, Credit Union, Smithsonian Early Enrichment Center (Child Care), Flexible Spending Account (Health & Dependent Care).

Conditions of Employment

• Pass Pre-employment Background Check and Subsequent Background Investigation for position designated.

• Complete a Probationary Period.

• Maintain a Bank Account for Direct Deposit/Electronic Transfer.

• The position is open to all candidates eligible to work in the United States. Proof of eligibility to work in U.S. is not required to apply.

• Applicants must meet all qualification and eligibility requirements within 30 days of the closing date of this announcement.

OVERVIEW
This position is located in Washington, DC, within the Forest Global Earth Observatory (ForestGEO), Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute (STRI), under the Office of the Under Secretary for Science and Research at the Smithsonian Institution (SI).

STRI provides a global platform for research on tropical forests and marine ecosystems, biodiversity, and human well-being.

The ForestGEO program is a global network of scientists and forest research sites dedicated to advancing the long-term study of the world's forests.

The GEO-TREES initiative builds on this network to improve the accuracy and verification of global forest carbon estimates through collaboration among forest research sites worldwide. The Data Scientist supports the Forest Global Earth Observatory (ForestGEO) and GEO-TREES programs as a liaison between site-based data collection and the development of analytical data products.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Data Management, Scientific Analysis, and Software Programming (50%)

• Performs data-management, computational, and bioinformatics assignments supporting research in tropical biology, ecology, and forestry.

• Develops, implements, modifies, and maintains data-processing pipelines used to process plot-based tree inventory and related ecological data and to derive estimates such as forest woody biomass density.

• Evaluates the performance of existing data-processing pipelines and recommends modifications or improvements based on data characteristics, analytical requirements, user needs, and experience working with ForestGEO and GEO-TREES site teams.

• Develops and modifies computational procedures for analysis of ForestGEO and GEO-TREES scientific data using established data-science principles, methods, and practices.

• Processes, validates, organizes, and manages tree inventory, Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS), Airborne Laser Scanning (ALS), and Terrestrial Laser Scanning (TLS) data for scientific analysis and long-term storage.

• Supports the archiving and long-term management of scientific datasets to ensure appropriate organization, documentation, accessibility, and usability.

• Develops and maintains data-management solutions and informatics workflows for data acquisition, formatting, validation, processing, analysis, use, and storage.

• Implements established data standards and contributes to the development and modification of data structures and architectures appropriate to assigned projects.

• Writes, tests, documents, troubleshoots, and maintains computer code used in data-processing and analytical workflows.

• Uses programming languages and tools such as R, Python, SQL, Git, GitHub, GIS applications, and related scientific and data-management software.

• Identifies data-quality problems, inconsistencies, missing values, formatting issues, and other anomalies and determines appropriate methods for correcting or documenting them.

• Works with researchers and other technical personnel to ensure that processed data and analyticalproducts meet established scientific and program requirements.

Requirements Gathering and Technical Support (25%)

• Works closely with researchers and program personnel to identify data-processing, analytical, software, and data-management requirements for assigned scientific projects.

• Conducts technical analyses of available methods and alternatives and recommends appropriate software tools, workflows, calculations, and analytical approaches.

• Assists researchers in translating scientific requirements into practical data-processing and

• computational solutions.

• Evaluates existing workflows and recommends modifications when established approaches do not fully address the characteristics of the data or requirements of an assigned project.

• Coordinates with site representatives concerning timelines and technical requirements for acquisition and submission of plot inventory, TLS, ALS, GNSS, and related scientific data.

• Reviews submitted data to determine whether established ForestGEO and GEO-TREES formatting, documentation, and data-quality requirements have been met.

• Works with site personnel to resolve routine and moderately complex data-submission and data-quality problems.

• Coordinates with the Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) and other appropriate technical staff to ensure assigned development activities follow applicable systems-development, documentation, version-control, security, and software-development practices.

• Prepares technical documentation describing data-processing workflows, code, data structures, analytical procedures, and related methods.

• Assists in testing new or modified software tools, workflows, and procedures prior to implementation.

Training and Collaboration (25%)

• Develops and provides formal and informal training to researchers, site personnel, and program partners concerning ForestGEO and GEO-TREES data systems, data-management procedures, formatting requirements, data-processing workflows, and related tools.

• Serves as a technical point of contact for tree-inventory teams and other users at assigned ForestGEO and GEO-TREES sites.

• Provides advice, training, troubleshooting assistance, and technical support concerning data collection, formatting, cleaning, validation, processing, documentation, and submission.

• Explains data standards, analytical procedures, software requirements, and data-management practices to researchers and partners with varying levels of technical expertise.

• Collaborates with scientists, data managers, programmers, and other personnel to identify and resolve data-management and processing problems.

• Participates in meetings, working groups, and collaborative activities involving ForestGEO, GEO-TREES, Smithsonian staff, and domestic and international research partners.

• Shares information concerning lessons learned, recurring data problems, workflow improvements, and effective data-management practices with program staff and partners.

Performs other duties as assigned.

QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS
Education and Experience:

• Professional knowledge of and skill in applying a wide range of data-science principles, concepts, methods, and practices sufficient to perform difficult data-management, processing, computational, and analytical assignments involving ecological and forestry data.

• Knowledge of data acquisition, data cleaning, validation, transformation, integration, storage, analysis, visualization, documentation, and reproducible computational workflows.

• Knowledge of computational and data-management methods is required to develop, modify, implement, and maintain processing pipelines for tree inventory, GNSS, ALS, TLS, spatial, and related scientific datasets.

• Knowledge of programming concepts and skill in applying programming languages and analytical tools such as R, Python, SQL, Git, GitHub, and related software to manipulate, process, analyze, and manage scientific data.

• Knowledge of algorithm development, software testing, version control, debugging, documentation, deployment, and maintenance practices is required to support scientific applications and data-processing workflows.

• Knowledge of spatial-data concepts, common spatial-data formats, and GIS software is required to process and evaluate geospatial information associated with ForestGEO and GEO-TREES projects.

• Knowledge of the scientific concepts associated with ecology, tropical biology, forestry, or related environmental sciences sufficient to understand data characteristics, research requirements, analytical objectives, and the relationships among data variables.

• Knowledge to select and modify appropriate data-processing and analytical methods; identify and resolve data-quality problems; evaluate alternative computational approaches; interpret results; develop recommendations; and prepare technical documentation and analytical products.

• Skill adapting or modifying established data-science techniques and procedures to address differences in data structure, quality, collection methods, analytical requirements, or site-specific circumstances.

Job Description Summary:
As a Senior Business Data Analyst, you will serve as a senior analytics partner and business intelligence subject matter expert, helping offices across the institution transform complex data into meaningful, actionable insights by conducting analysis, visualizing data, providing context, and helping stakeholders understand trends, performance, risks, and opportunities. In this role, you will work closely with leadership and staff to define business questions, clarify analytical needs, develop trusted data assets, and create dashboards and reporting that support strategic decision-making. You will play a key role in expanding analytics support beyond the Office of the Chief Financial Officer to institutional partners such as the Office of Strategy and Engagement, the Office of Peer Review, and the National Research Council Executive Office.

Job Description:

ESSENTIAL JOB DUTIES

Duties may be performed solely for a specific business or functional area or a combination of areas.

Institutional Analytics and Stakeholder Partnership: Partners with leadership and staff across institutional units to understand business needs, define analytical questions, clarify reporting goals, identify relevant metrics, assess available data, and determine the most effective analytical approach. Conducts analysis to identify trends, patterns, risks, opportunities, and key findings, and translates those findings into clear insights that support planning, operational improvement, performance tracking, and senior leadership decision-making.

Dashboard Development and Business Intelligence: Designs, builds, tests, publishes, and maintains dashboards and reporting products in Tableau and related business intelligence platforms. Creates dashboards that are accurate, accessible, visually clear, and aligned with stakeholder needs. Manages the release of assigned dashboards, including requirements gathering, stakeholder review, testing, documentation, publication, and post-release support.

Analytics Infrastructure: Develops and maintains a unified analytics foundation for Tableau by creating consistent structures, reusable data assets, transformation logic, and common business rules that allow data from multiple sources to be used reliably across Business Data Analytics products. Ensures that analytical workflows are sustainable, scalable, well-documented, structured in a way that supports consistent analysis, reduces duplication, and strengthens confidence in reported results and designed to support both current reporting needs and future growth.

Data Assets: Designs, builds, and maintains data assets in the Tableau data ecosystem for senior leadership decision support by ensuring the overall accuracy, completeness, and reliability of datasets and data models.

Data Quality: Supports strong data quality practices within Business Data Analytics by helping ensure that key metrics, definitions, assumptions, and business rules are applied consistently across analytics products. Identifies and communicates data quality issues, source system limitations, and interpretation considerations that may affect reporting or decision-making. Contributes to clear, transparent use of data with documentation.

Consultation: Provides expert guidance to stakeholders on data interpretation, reporting approaches and analytical best practices. Supports technical components of dashboard development such as consulting on coding buildout.

Staff Management: May train and coach analytical staff. If supervising staff, provides leadership and mentors employees. Trains and develops employees to successfully perform current responsibilities and encourages development of staff for future roles. Forms effective teams and cultivates a work environment that fosters teamwork. Interprets and ensures consistent application of organizational policies. Initiates personnel actions, including performance and compensation reviews and disciplinary actions. Mentors, collaborates with, and advises data analytics team members.

Confidentiality: Maintains an appropriate standard of confidentiality. Maintains strict confidence and exercises care when handling secure, privileged, sensitive, or confidential information and matters to prevent disclosure to others. Accesses confidential information for work-related reasons only, following the policies and procedures of the organization. Ensures that any privileged, sensitive, or confidential information is securely stored, disposed of, and transmitted according to the Institutional guidance.

NONESSENTIAL JOB DUTIES
• Related duties and special projects as assigned.

JOB SPECIFICATIONS

Required Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities: Thorough knowledge of up-to-date data analysis techniques. Deep understanding of utilization of data analysis and visualization tools, platforms, and software (i.e., Tableau). Above average to advance level computer skills which may include SQL, Excel and Google Analytics. Abilities to manage data pipelines for highly complex data. Strong organizational, problem-solving, and presentation skills. Excellent attention to detail. Ability to meet deadlines in a fast-paced office environment during peak periods. Ability to manage and maintain privileged, sensitive, and confidential information and matters appropriately. Ability to solve non-routine intellectual problems of substantial variety and complexity using originality and ingenuity. Serves as a resource to others in the resolution of complex problems. Ability to use substantial latitude for independent judgment and action. Experience working in complex environments with a high degree of organizational effectiveness. Ability to successfully work in a team environment and to form and maintain effective teams. Ability to develop relationships with co-workers and employees in other National Academies’ departments through effective communication. Excellent communication skills with a proven ability to effectively interact with all levels of employees.

Minimum Education/Training Requirements: Bachelor’s Degree in relevant field or related field, or equivalent knowledge. Master’s Degree is preferred.

Minimum Experience: Six years of related professional experience. Tableau, data analysis, and visualizations is required. Advanced experience in Tableau Desktop and Tableau Prep is required. Experience with Snowflake preferred.

Physical Capabilities: Ability to work at a computer for extended periods of time.

Required Licenses, Certification or Registration: None.

Supervisory Responsibilities/Controls: Reports to Director of Business Data Analytics. General direction is provided. May supervise staff.

Work Environment: Office environment with occasional travel between National Academies’ facilities and to off-site locations. Additional hours may be required to support internal and external deadlines during peak periods. 60% telework eligible.

Compensation & Benefits: An estimated compensation range for this position is $92,040 - $126,550. Compensation offered to the selected candidate will be based on the candidate’s relevant knowledge, skills, and work experience, commensurate with compensation of current employees in comparable positions with similar knowledge, skills, and work experience, and subject to budget parameters. Note it is not typical for a candidate to be hired at the higher end of the range. This is a benefits-eligible position. Manager Data Engineering/Architect, Data Engineering

As a Manager Data Engineering/Data Architect, you will be responsible for designing, building, and optimizing data platforms that enable scalable, high-performance data processing and analytics. You will work closely with cross-functional teams to develop and implement data solutions that drive business insights and innovation.

Your Impact:

• Combine your technical expertise and problem-solving passion to work closely with clients, turning complex ideas into end-to-end data solutions that transform our clients’ business.
• Translate client requirements into system design and develop solutions that deliver measurable business value.
• Lead, design, develop and deliver large-scale data systems, data processing, data transformation, and data platform modernization initiatives.
• Build and optimize batch and streaming data pipelines across modern cloud data platforms and distributed processing frameworks.
• Support AI-enabled engineering use cases by designing high-quality data foundations, retrieval patterns, context engineering approaches, and scalable data services that power agentic and machine learning solutions.
• Automate data platform operations and manage post-production systems, observability, quality, reliability, and operational processes, including telemetry pipelines that capture prompt, response, trace, latency, token, and cost data for AI-enabled services in a queryable form.
• Conduct technical feasibility assessments and provide project estimates for the design and development of solutions.
• Mentor, support, and grow junior team members while contributing hands-on to delivery.

Your Skills & Experience:

• Demonstrable experience implementing end-to-end data pipelines and production-grade data platforms.
• Hands-on experience with at least one leading public cloud data platform: Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud Platform;
• Experience with Databricks as a data engineering platform is strongly preferred, including working with notebooks, jobs, Delta Lake, or similar lakehouse patterns.
• Strong Python proficiency and practical experience using Python-based tooling for data engineering, automation, platform development, or AI engineering workflows.
• Implementation experience with column-oriented database technologies such as BigQuery, Redshift, Vertica, or similar platforms; NoSQL database technologies such as DynamoDB, Bigtable, Cosmos DB, or similar; and traditional database systems such as SQL Server, Oracle, or MySQL.
• Experience implementing data pipelines for both streaming and batch integrations using tools and frameworks such as Glue ETL, Lambda, Google Cloud Dataflow, Azure Data Factory, Spark, Spark Streaming, or similar technologies.
• Experience with data modeling, warehouse design, fact/dimension implementations, and modern lakehouse or data mesh patterns.
• Experience with code repositories, continuous integration, automated testing, release management, and production support practices.
• Familiarity with MLOps concepts and the data engineering responsibilities required to support AI/ML deployment, validation, monitoring, rollback, and operational reliability.
• Ability to handle module or track-level responsibilities while contributing to tasks hands-on.
• Good communication skills and willingness to work as part of a collaborative, cross-functional team.

AI Engineering & Modern Data Platform Experience:

• Exposure to AI engineering patterns, including context engineering, retrieval-augmented generation support patterns, agent architectures, and production data services that support AI-enabled experiences.
• Experience building and maintaining the pipelines behind retrieval systems, including document parsing, chunking, metadata extraction, embedding generation, and incremental reindexing, alongside the vector databases, graph databases, semantic search, and knowledge retrieval structures they feed.
• Exposure to agentic platforms or cloud AI services such as Vertex AI, Azure AI services, AWS AI services, or comparable platforms; specific platform experience is less important than understanding how AI engineering differs from traditional data engineering.
• Practical experience deploying agents, integrating agent frameworks, or supporting agentic workflows in production or near-production environments is a plus.
• Experience building evaluation data infrastructure for AI systems, including ground-truth and golden datasets, offline evaluation pipelines, and the data scaffolding behind LLM-as-judge and regression testing.
• Experience modeling and persisting agent state, including session context, conversation history, and memory stores, treating them as a durable storage and data modeling problem rather than an application detail.
• Support AI-enabled engineering use cases by designing high-quality data foundations, retrieval patterns, context engineering approaches, and scalable data services that power agentic and machine learning solutions, applying the same lineage, provenance, and data contract rigor to context and retrieval sources that you would to a production warehouse.
• Experience with agentic harnesses or orchestration tools such as Pi, Hermes Agent, or similar platforms is a plus, but not required.
• Experience with Snowflake and zero-copy architecture patterns is a plus, particularly for retail, financial services, energy, or CPG-oriented use cases.

Set Yourself Apart With:

• Developer certifications for AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, Databricks, Snowflake, or related cloud/data platforms.
• Demonstrated experience applying AI engineering concepts in practical business environments rather than only academic or research settings.
• Hands-on experience supporting AI/ML and LLM lifecycle needs such as model deployment support, monitoring, validation, shadow deployments, release management, and evaluation or data quality measurement for both predictive models and generative systems.
• Experience in retail, financial services, energy, CPG, logistics, manufacturing, or other data-rich industries where applied AI and large-scale data engineering are used to solve operational or client-facing problems.
• Understanding of Agile, product, and delivery methodologies in consulting or client-facing environments.

Additional Information

• An inclusive workplace that promotes diversity and collaboration.
• Access to ongoing learning and development opportunities.
• Competitive compensation and benefits package.
• Flexibility to support work-life balance.
• Comprehensive health benefits for you and your family.
• Generous paid leave and holidays.
• Wellness program and employee assistance.
